title: How Database Indexes Actually Work — Why the Same Query Can Take 2ms or 8 Seconds
subtitle: The phone book analogy that actually explains it, and how to find the problem with EXPLAIN
excerpt: The same query on the same table can take milliseconds or seconds depending entirely on whether the database has an index to use. Here's what an index actually does, and when adding one hurts more than it helps.
metaDescription: How database indexes actually work — why unindexed queries do a full table scan, when adding an index helps versus hurts, and how to use EXPLAIN to diagnose a slow query.
author: Muthu

faq.question: Should I just add an index to every column to be safe?
faq.answer: No — every index slows down writes (inserts, updates, deletes) because it has to be maintained on every change. Index columns that are actually used often in WHERE, JOIN, or ORDER BY; leave the rest alone, especially on small tables or low-variation columns.
